claim: voucher() builds a root voucher from whatever single root private the keyfile holds without checking that its kid names a root the atSign publishes, so a leftover private writes root links that read broken, and linkKeysOf/_replaces lets those overwrite anchored chain links.
mechanism: voucher() (pq_signing_chain.dart:559-570) takes PqSigningRoot.signingKey() and returns LinkVoucher.root whenever kid != null and isFullyPrivileged(). signingKey (pq_signing_root.dart:560-587) gets the private from _signingPrivate, which returns the only active private without any correspondence check when one is held (pq_signing_root.dart:857-858). It then names that private by the kid of its filed public half (583-584), even though it has just read `roots` (567) and that kid may not be among them; the new fallback only runs when no public half is filed. In linkKeysOf (652-703), _replaces (772-783) returns voucher.isRoot == true for any found chain link without walking it. So the stale-signed root link is sent with expect = that chain link, and for a key with no link it is sent with expect null. The atServer stores links without checking signatures (docs/projects/pq/acceptance.md 18.2 'Forgery'). walkFrom (425-446) then finds no published root with that kid; the link is root-shaped, so it reads ChainVerdict.broken. The base code had a receiver-side guard that this PR removes: _stampRootLink verified a conveyed root link against the published root before stamping it, which kept such links off other enrollments. This breaks UC-G3.19 ('a root link only by the root').
repro: Fully privileged client F mints a root. Its publish loses to another enrollment's root R, and either the retire of the losing pair fails (pq_signing_root.dart:412-418, logged 'until a later start retires it, this enrollment wrongly reads as holding the root') or the record cannot be read after the failed write, so the pair is kept (389-399). F's keyfile now holds one active root private P, with its public half, that matches no published root. Before F's start reconciles it, F approves enrollment N, for example with at_activate approve while the unawaited startup is still running. _linkKeysOf -> voucher -> signingKey returns (P, kid(P)) because roots == [R] is non-empty -> LinkVoucher.root -> enroll:link writes root links naming kid(P) on N's keys. anchoring(N) then reads 'broken <kid>' rather than anchored (if F had an anchored key, a chain voucher would have been used) or unsigned, and N cannot vouch for anything until another root holder sweeps it. If P stays active because the retire keeps failing, F's sweep (voucher.isRoot) also replaces every other enrollment's anchored chain link with a broken root link.

claim: The approval tests' privilege fake gives the same answer for the approver's own privilege and for enrollment B's, so no at_client unit test notices if the link step decides root links on B's privilege instead of the approver's.
mechanism: _FakePrivilege (approve_link_flavour_test.dart:17-26) returns `answer` from both isFullyPrivileged() and isEnrollmentFullyPrivileged(id). Even so, _FakePrivilege(true) reports it as fully privileged in the test at :124-150 and in the other root-holder tests (:226, :244, :265, :297, :331). _FakePrivilege(false) in the test at :152-172 makes the approver and B indistinguishable. So no test sees a case where the approver's privilege and B's differ. pq_signing_chain_test and chain_sweep_test call voucher/linkKeysOf directly rather than through _linkKeysOf. enrollment_conveyance_guard_test's _AlwaysPrivileged approvers hold no voucher, so _linkKeysOf returns before the question is asked. A grep for enroll:link/LinkVoucher across package tests finds no other test of the approval link step. Only the CI functional pack's UC-G3.5 root arm (tests/at_functional_test/test/per_key_links_live_test.dart:144-157, a fully privileged root holder approving a scoped B and expecting a one-hop root link) would catch the swap.
repro: Change envelope_enrollment_conveyance.dart:213 to `isFullyPrivileged: () => _privilege.isEnrollmentFullyPrivileged(id)`. Every test in approve_link_flavour_test.dart still passes: _FakePrivilege(true) still yields root links, and _FakePrivilege(false) still yields no enroll:link. The production effect would be this. A fully privileged root holder approving a namespace-scoped enrollment, the usual case, would chain-link it through its own key, or link nothing if it has none, instead of root-linking it. A root-private holder that is not fully privileged, approving a fully privileged enrollment, would sign root links, against UC-G3.19. A fake that answered isEnrollmentFullyPrivileged from the target's grants (false for scoped-1), or recorded calls to it as pq_client_bootstrap_test's fake does, would turn the test at :124-150 red.

v.reason: Every element of the mechanism traces through the real source. Test 4 asserts only the keyfile end-state and the absence of ':rootlink' events. Since this PR, _anchorOwnKeys reconciles the held private against the published root via mintIfAbsent -> _reconcileAgainstPublished -> _retireUnadvertised for a fully privileged client (the fixture's e-1 qualifies), so the retirement assertion holds whatever the hydrate step did; and the ':rootlink' assertion can never fail for this orphan because its kid is null either way (no filed public half, no corresponding published root) or it is already retired. Under the repro's reorder, hydrateStore primes the orphan into the in-memory secret store before reconcileHeldPrivate retires it from the keyfile, and inbound pulls for the root are served from that store with no check that the holder still holds the material; nothing in the startup removes the primed entry, and a pulling enrollment discards the orphan after its broadcast is spent. No test observes the offer: test 1's hydrate marker is the reconcile's record read (still before the sweep under the reorder), no bootstrap test hydrates an orphan, and the fixture's only enrollment is the client itself, so the serve never fires as a wire observable. The test therefore passes while the orphan is offered, as claimed. The only element I could not check is the pre-PR git history ("publishOwnRootLink did not reconcile and signed even with a null kid") — no git data available in the checkout — but that is historical framing; the operative claim about the current tree holds entirely.
